newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ALNA SELLS $2 MLN SHARE ISSUE TO HANSA - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ALNA SELLS $2 MLN SHARE ISSUE TO HANSA - REPORT.

text.p: Lithuania's information technologies company Alna issued a new $2 million share issue and sold it to Hansa Investments, the investment arm of Estonia's Hansa Group, the newspaper Verslo Zinios reported.
Hansa Investments sold part of the shares to the investment fund Baltic Republic Fund and Mercury Asset Management, based in London, the newspaper said.
Twenty-one percent of the company is controlled by foreign capital now, the newspaper said, and 73 percent is owned by Alna staff.

Alna Director General, Valentinas Milaknis, was quoted as saying that the company should be listed on the Vilnius bourse before March 31, 1998, after the closed stock company is reorganised into a public company.

The chairman of Hansa Investments, Joakim Helenius, was quoted as saying that it was the first project implemented by the company in Lithuania and that they are continuing to look for companies to invest in.
Alna posted a 1.5 million litas net profit in 1996 on a turnover of 33.5 million litas.
The company forecasts three million litas net profit for 1997 and a turnover 48 million litas in 1997.
